claims.text: AI Agents are modular, single-entity systems driven by LLMs and Large Image Models (LIMs) designed for task-specific automation within bounded environments.
Agentic AI systems represent a paradigm shift marked by multi-agent collaboration, dynamic task decomposition, persistent memory, and coordinated autonomy.
Tool augmentation with function calling enables LLM-based agents to access real-time information and execute multi-step external workflows.
ReAct loops integrate iterative reasoning, action execution, and observation steps to reduce logical errors and hallucinations in agent execution.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds agent decisions in external vector databases to expand knowledge beyond static LLM pretraining cutoffs.
Multi-agent AI architectures are vulnerable to inter-agent error cascades where a single agent's false output corrupts downstream decisions.

evidence.description: The authors define AI Agents as modular systems driven and enabled by LLMs and LIMs operating automatically within explicitly defined scopes.
Agentic AI systems are defined as orchestrated multi-agent ecosystems utilizing goal decomposition, persistent memory, and shared context channels.
Function calling formats structured JSON/SQL requests routed through orchestration layers to execute external tool calls and feed results back into the LLM context window.
The ReAct pattern introduces an iterative loop where agents reason about tasks, invoke tools, and observe outcomes before taking subsequent steps.
RAG connects agents to vector stores such as FAISS and Pinecone, grounding outputs in retrieved domain knowledge to overcome static training data limits.
An erroneous or hallucinated validation output from one agent propagates through the network, corrupting subsequent summarizers or decision-makers.

methodologies.name: Hybrid Literature Discovery and Literature Review Strategy
methodologies.description: A multi-stage review methodology querying twelve academic databases and AI tools using targeted Boolean keyword combinations.
conditions: Boolean query combinations of AI Agents, Agentic AI, LLM Agents, Tool-augmented LLMs, and Multi-Agent AI Systems

methodologies.name: Multi-Dimensional Conceptual Taxonomy Framework
methodologies.description: A structural taxonomy comparing Generative AI, AI Agents, Agentic AI, and Generative Agents across architecture, operational mechanisms, complexity, interaction, and autonomy.
conditions: Categorical comparison across core function, primary driver, memory usage, orchestration, and task scope

limitations.text: This review adopts a sequential, layered architectural taxonomy rather than structuring the study around formal research questions typical of systematic literature reviews.
Existing survey literature frequently conflates AI Agents and Agentic AI under the generic term intelligent agents, causing conceptual ambiguity and misaligned system design.
LLM-based single AI agents lack genuine causal reasoning, making them brittle under distributional shifts and prone to hallucinations and prompt sensitivity.
Agentic AI systems suffer from high coordination overhead, communication bottlenecks, emergent instability, and a lack of formal verification methodologies.

future_work.text: Integration of causal inference models, Bayesian networks, or symbolic planning languages (e.g., PDDL) into agent architectures to enable counterfactual reasoning.
Establishment of standardized inter-agent communication protocols and interoperability standards (such as the Agent-to-Agent A2A protocol) across vendors.
Development of data-free, self-evolving reasoning frameworks operating through reinforced self-play without reliance on human-annotated datasets.
Creation of governance-aware architectures incorporating role isolation, traceable decision logging, and formal auditing mechanisms for safety-critical domains.
